# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

If session is null now (resumed without session?), `recordId != null` → unawaited(_writeSteringConsumed) skipped — hmm, `if (session != null)` inside `if (recordId != null)`. If session went null (session switch), the marker isn't written to the OLD session — the record stays unconsumed in the old session file → resurrection if the user resumes it later. Edge — session switch mid-drop. Pre-existing pattern for markers (`_steringDelivered` has the same `session == null → return` guard). Digest at most.

```dart

``

For an entry with persistError == null and recordId == null — in-flight write. The drop prints "the text is lost" — but the in-flight write may land afterward and the resolution branch (index < 0) writes the consumed marker. So text NOT lost. The warning is a false claim in that race. They claim it can't be observed at SETLE time specifically — in their test the hold releases before settle because boundaries serialize behind the file lock. But conceptually with a 2s hold and an immediate settle... whatever. The race: settle drains + drops while an append is parked → prints "text is lost" → append lands → marker written → text survived. The message lied. It's an honesty race in an edge case; the code at least prints SOMETHING (vs old silent drop). The card's own "Remaining" section acknowledges this. Setle-run branch: `await _retrySteringPersist(entry)` → append lands (recordId R). `unawaited(_steringDelivered(...R))` → writes marker for R. Meanwhile the original failed persist is done (it failed — no pending resolution). No double.

Scenario: entry in flight (no error, no id) at boundary merge. `_persistIncremental`: `await _retrySteringPersist(entry)` → null (persistError null) → `_steringDelivered(message, null, panel)` — no marker. All 114 tests pass (112 REG + the new suite — actually +114). `dart analyze` clean on the touched files.

Importantly, `_startRun` has a busy guard: "a run is already streaming — wait for it to settle... then retry". So the race I was worried about (setle microtask `_startRun` clobbering a user-started run) — if the user starts a run in the microtask window, the settle's `_startRun` will refuse (isBusy → dim note). But wait: is that reachable and is the leftover steering then LOST?

Scenario: run A settles → whenComplete fires → `unawaited(_setleLeftoverStering())`. The settle's synchronous part: drain queue, reconcile, removeWhere, writeln('stering arrived after the last checkpoint — running N message(s) now'). Then the first `await _retrySteringPersist(entry)` suspends. In that gap, the user submits a new prompt → `_runPrompt` → `_startRun` → `_runStarting = true` / busy. The settle microtask resumes → completes loop → `_startRun(texts.join('\n'))` → isBusy → **refused with "a run is already streaming"**. The leftover steering: entries were already consumed (panels delivered via `_steringDelivered`, records marked consumed), and the texts are NOT in the new run's prompt — the run was started with the USER's text only. The steering text never gets run! Old behavior: `_setleLeftoverStering()` ran synchronously → `_startRun` called synchronously in the same whenComplete body — the user could not interleave between settle and settle-run (single synchronous block... well, the event loop couldn't process user input in between).

Hmm wait — actually let me re-check: the await gap. In the settle-run branch:

```dart
for (final entry in entries) {
 final recordId = await _retrySteringPersist(entry);
 unawaited(_steringDelivered(entry.message, recordId, entry.panel));
}
_startRun(texts.join('\n'));
``

`_retrySteringPersist(entry)`:
- If entry.recordId != null → async fn, returns completed future — but `await` still yields to the microtask queue! So even the healthy path suspends. Between suspend and resume, other microtasks AND macro-events (user input via stdin handler) can run.

So the window: between the settle's `writeln('stering arrived...')` and `_startRun(...)`, there is at least one microtask hop per entry (healthy entries) or a full session-append (retry entries). During that window, a user submit (macro-event) can start a run. Then `_startRun(texts.join)` hits the busy guard → refuses → the stered texts are consumed (markers written, panels delivered, FIFO drained) but never delivered into any run. Worse: the messages were already drained from the agent queue. The texts are LOST — silently, except the "running N message(s) now" line that lied (the run never started), plus the busy-guard dim note.

How likely is a user submit in that microtask window? Microtask hops are sub-millisecond normally; a user typing at the exact settle moment is unlikely but possible (this is precisely the "stering arrived after the last checkpoint" edge — racing human input). The old code had NO await between settle detection and `_startRun` — the window was zero (synchronous block). The async change opens it.

Also — even without user input: what else runs during those microtask hops? The `whenComplete` body continues: `unawaited(_waiting.push())`, `_writeIdlePrompt()`. No other `_startRun` triggers in the body. The inbox tick could fire `_wakeOnRecoveredStering` — guarded by `isBusy` and `_steringWakeRunning`... and `_startRun` from mail/scheduled messages (`agent_cli_inbox.dart:419`) — also a trigger. Same window.

Additionally, the busy-guard refusal is the SAFE behavior for interleaved runs generally — but here the settle branch has ALREADY consumed the FIFO entries and printed "running N message(s) now". The refusal note comes after. The texts never reach a run. That's a genuine (if narrow) regression: silent-ish steering loss in a race window that did not exist before (before, the settle-run decision and `_startRun` were atomic).

Severity: this is a correctness issue on a path the change actually touches (the settle path IS the change). It causes potential message loss in a race — the very class of defect the card fixes (#2249 is about steering loss/honesty). I'd classify ⚠️ IMPORTANT — real correctness edge introduced by the async hop; probability low but consequence is exactly the lost-stering class the card is about, and the fix is easy (await nothing before `_startRun`: do the retry persists AFTER starting the run, or re-order `_startRun` before the per-entry awaits, or call `_startRun` synchronously first then fire deliveries).

Hmm wait — actually let me double check: is the loop's await truly reached before `_startRun` in the common (healthy) path? `entries` non-empty (there are leftovers). `_retrySteringPersist(entry)` — async function → even with a sync return, the caller awaits → yields. YES.

Could they have avoided the yield by calling `_startRun` before the loop? The order matters for the messages though: deliveries' transition lines print before the run's output starts. Reordering `_startRun` first would change copy ordering (transition lines would interleave with run output) — but correctness first. Alternative: keep the loop but run it AFTER `_startRun` (deliveries are unawaited anyway). Or make `_retrySteringPersist` a sync-decision + async-append... The fix shape is for the author; my job is to flag it.

Is it BLOCKING? Criteria: merge would cause a bug. It WOULD cause a rare bug (stering loss). But probability is low and the consequence bounded (text lost, honest-ish messages mixed). The old code ALSO could lose steering in races (that's what the card fixes; "raced past the last poll"). Let me be careful: was there an equivalent window pre-change? arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: "the text is lost" can be false while the accept-append is still parked**

In `_dropSettledSteering`, the in-flight shape (`recordId == null && persistError == null`) prints `save still in flight` and then the unconditional `the text is lost` claim:

```dart
final why = entry.persistError == null
    ? 'save still in flight'   // line 473
    : 'fs error: ${entry.persistError}';
io.writeln(tuiWarning('⚠ dropped steering was NOT saved to session ($why) — the text is lost:'));
```

But `_retrySteeringPersist` returns `null` for this shape **without touching the session** (the `persistError == null` early-return performs no writer-serialized call), so nothing orders the drop print behind the parked append. When the parked append lands a moment later, the persist resolution's `index < 0` branch writes the consumed marker — the text survived, closed, no resurrection — yet the user was told it is lost.

The card's Remaining section argues this state is unobservable "from a black-box test" under writer serialization, but the drop branch itself does no serialized write for this entry shape, so the claim doesn't hold: a slow fs (#2248's bounded session-IO) makes it reachable in production, and the suite's own `_SteeringFsGateEnv.holdSessionWrites` across the settle can arrange it deterministically (the AC2/AC3 tests park appends for 2s across boundaries already).

Copy-only, no data impact — hence a suggestion. Either soften the in-flight copy (e.g. "save still in flight — if it lands it will be marked consumed; check the record before retyping") or await the parked resolution (bounded by the same session-IO bound) before claiming loss.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The honest-persist and identity-settle work is solid and fully tested (114/114 steering-suite tests green, `dart analyze` and `dart format` clean on the touched files on this host; AC1–AC5 each have a pinned test). One important issue: the now-async settle can lose already-consumed steering texts when a competing run starts during the persist-retry window (`_startRun` refused by the busy guard after the FIFO was drained and "running N message(s) now" printed), plus one suggestion on a drop-branch copy line that can claim a loss the parked append later prevents.

**Key Issues**:
1. ⚠️ `agent_cli_steering.dart:404` — settle-run starts the follow-up run only *after* awaiting a persist re-attempt per entry; a submit/mail/scheduled run started in that window makes `_startRun` refuse, and the texts are gone (see inline thread).
2. 💡 `agent_cli_steering.dart:473` — `the text is lost` can be false for the in-flight-append shape; the drop branch performs no writer-serialized call for it, so the parked append can land right after the claim (see inline thread).

**Digest** (ranked overflow, not threads):
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart:467` — 🪶 unreachable `if (entry.recordId != null) continue;`: `_retrySteeringPersist` already returns `entry.recordId` when non-null, so the check only executes with `entry.recordId == null`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_steering.dart:321` — 💡 `_retrySteeringPersist` swallows the retry's own error at the boundary-merge delivery attempt; the accept-time warning told the truth once, but the retry failure gets no print (the drop branch prints its retry failure — parity gap).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_input.dart:217` — 🪶 the async settle lets `_writeIdlePrompt()` render before the follow-up run starts; cosmetic idle-flash ordering vs the pre-change synchronous `_startRun`.

**Next Steps**:
1. Start the settle-run synchronously before the per-entry persist retries (or re-check `isBusy` after the awaits and loudly re-drop instead of consuming-and-losing).
2. Soften the in-flight drop copy or await the parked resolution before claiming loss.
3. Sweep the three digest items if convenient — none blocks merge.

All checks pass. The review is complete.

## Review summary — PR #2253 (`fix/2249-steering-persist-lies`)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (1 ⚠️ IMPORTANT, 1 💡 SUGGESTION, 3 digest lines, 0 blocking).

**What I verified on this host**: `dart pub get` + `dart analyze` clean on all 12 touched files (the 78 repo-level errors are pre-existing `office_addin/` package-resolution noise), `dart format` clean, and the full steering suite + all 9 REG suites the PR lists ran green — **114/114 passed**.

**Findings**:
1. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`agent_cli_steering.dart:404`) — the settle is now `unawaited`/async and the settle-run branch awaits a persist re-attempt per entry **before** `_startRun`. In that window (microtask hop for healthy entries; a full session append up to the #2248 IO bound for `persistError` entries) a competing composer submit/mail/scheduled run can start; the settle's `_startRun` then hits the busy guard and refuses — **after** the FIFO was drained, panels flipped delivered, and "running N message(s) now" was printed. The texts end up in no run and no queue — silent steering loss behind a lying announce line, exactly the defect class the card closes. Pre-change this block was synchronous (no window). Fix: start the run first, or re-check `isBusy` after the awaits and re-drop loudly.
2. 💡 **SUGESTION** (`agent_cli_steering.dart:473`) — the drop branch's `the text is lost` claim can be false for the in-flight-append shape: `_retrySteeringPersist` returns null *without* a writer-serialized call, so nothing orders the print behind the parked append; when it lands, the `index < 0` resolution writes the marker and the text survived. Copy-only; the card's "unobservable" note doesn't hold for the drop path (slow fs / the suite's own `holdSessionWrites` gate).
3. **Digest**: unreachable `if (entry.recordId != null) continue;` (:467), silent retry-failure swallow in `_retrySteeringPersist` (:321, parity gap with the drop branch), idle-prompt render ordering vs the async settle (`agent_cli_input.dart:217`).

The core work is sound: the identity zip correctly closes the same-text double-delivery hole (verified against `_PendingMessageQueue` oneAtATime semantics and the spill-guard identity preservation), `steeringSaveClause` keeps the #437 healthy copy byte-identical, `aborted` state reuse is correct, and every AC (1–5) has a pinned test that passed here.

Artifacts written: `outputs/pr_review.json`, `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md` (no `response.md`, per contract).
